Both series normalized to 0 at tau=-1
Red series (missing jobs Delta_b) drops sharply to approx -0.022 at tau=0 and persists negative through tau=+4
Blue series (excess jobs Delta_a) jumps sharply to approx +0.024 at tau=0 and persists positive through tau=+4
95% confidence-interval error bars on every point
Dashed vertical reference line at tau=0
Pretreatment leads (tau=-2, tau=-3) near zero / statistically indistinguishable from zero
y-axis range approx -0.04 to +0.04; color-coded red vs blue series

rationale: The exact expected file figures/figures/Figure3.pdf exists and was regenerated by this run (replication_log.json lists it as an output of step 2, which ports Table1_for_QJE.do / makefigure_massovertime to R; fix_severity.json shows only 'major' environment-port fixes and no critical fix in this path). Reading the PDF confirms all structural features of the claim: an event-study plot over annualized event time -3 to +4 with both series pinned to 0 at tau=-1; a red series for missing jobs (Delta_b) that breaks sharply downward to about -0.022 at tau=0 and stays negative (about -0.013 to -0.019) through tau=+4; a blue series for excess jobs (Delta_a) that jumps to about +0.024 at tau=0 and stays positive (about +0.017 to +0.022) through tau=+4; 95% CI error bars on every point; a dashed vertical line at tau=0; and pretreatment leads (tau=-2) essentially on zero with CIs straddling zero. Magnitudes, directions, sharp break at tau=0, persistence over five years, and near-zero leads all match the claim. The only deviation is cosmetic: the red (below) line is drawn solid rather than dashed as the paper text describes, which does not affect interpretation since color-coding separates the series.
